correctness.rationale: For a fixed interior restart point and every 0<alpha<2pi the Brownian wedge kernel yields equal leading free boundary currents of index beta+1. Integration gives each marked free survival tail. Exact defective renewal convolution and an early/late-time split yield each fixed-count marked asymptotic, including the tight random last-reset time. Independently, the threshold-count geometric random-sum representation, the regular-variation convolution law and a summable geometric union-bound envelope derive the total first-passage tail A0/a without assuming the November 2026 paper. Normalized fixed-count masses sum to one, proving tightness. Strong Markov restart gives the independent future geometric count. Limit-law moments and prefactor special cases pass finite algebraic checks, none of which substitute for the continuum proof.

originality.rationale: The pre-anchor 2025 threshold resetting framework (Biswas, Majumdar and Pal, first April 18 2025) and wedge exit kernel (Najeeb, Pal and Prasad, first May 7 2025) motivate this joint path observable. The later November 19 2026 Najeeb–Pal–Prasad direct threshold-reset wedge paper was inspected fully: it covers the unconditional survival tail and reset counts, and its equal free currents match the independently derived kernel. Neither reports the four-variable late-survivor conditional joint law, retrospective fair current-excursion exit mark, tight last-reset epoch and different eventual total count. Duvall’s general survivor-count mechanism for intermittent maps and single-big-jump principles cover marginal approaches, not the full marked Brownian result. Unstated stronger generic coverage remains a real priority risk.
residual_risks: A more general marked heavy-tail renewal theorem may contain this as an unstated immediate corollary; the two component marginal mechanisms are known.

value.rationale: Late-survival conditioning probes which resets happened before an unusually long search and how many remain to happen: the past-count law stays geometric, the current excursion side becomes fair even when unconditional wedge splitting is strongly biased, and the eventual count is a non-geometric explicit two-piece convolution. The tight last-reset epoch provides a structural pathwise localization statement. These jointly sharpen the physically motivated reset-count statistics beyond moments and identify a robust observational distinction between prior and future resets. The result is exact within a natural pure-threshold-reset submodel and makes no claim of experimental stability, finite-time error rate or broad new renewal mechanism.
